name: Solar Water Pumping
summary: Photovoltaic-powered water pumping systems that replace diesel or manual pumping for irrigation, livestock watering, and rural water supply.
description: Solar water pumping systems use photovoltaic (PV) panels to generate electricity that drives submersible or surface-mounted water pumps. The technology eliminates the need for diesel fuel or grid electricity, dramatically reducing operating costs over time. Systems range in scale from small (<1 kW) units for individual farmers or community water points, to large multi-kW arrays feeding irrigation distribution networks for hundreds of acres. In agri-energy applications, solar pumping is most commonly used for gravity-fed drip and sprinkler irrigation, livestock watering troughs, and community water supply in off-grid settings. System components include PV panels, a pump controller (MPPT or PWM), the pump unit, and often a storage tank to buffer supply. Direct pumping (pump runs during daylight, tank fills for use at night) is the simplest configuration. Battery-buffered systems allow pumping at any time but increase capital cost.
benefits: Eliminates diesel fuel operating costs after installation
Low maintenance compared to diesel pumps
Scalable — from 0.5 kW individual systems to 100+ kW schemes
Long service life (20+ years for PV panels)
limitations: Higher upfront capital cost than diesel pumps
Output depends on solar irradiance (reduced on cloudy days)
Requires adequate water source (river, borehole, dam)
Pump controller and pump components require periodic servicing
Sizing must account for peak demand and seasonal variation
operationalNotes: Size PV array based on peak water demand and local irradiance data
Include a storage tank (0.5 to 1 day supply) to buffer cloudy day output
Use MPPT controllers for best energy conversion efficiency
Ensure borehole yield testing before installation
Establish a water user group with a clear cost-recovery plan
maintenanceNotes: Clean PV panels weekly (especially in dry dusty conditions)
Inspect pump unit and rising main annually
Check electrical connections and cable glands each season
Keep a spare set of fuses and cable connectors on site
